name: "The Superstar" Joey Maxx
notes: Known from one segment of the USCW Flash Central of 5 May 1998, posted 6 May 1998 and served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/uscw-flash-central-5-5-98-pt-2-1998-05-06.html. Entering to "Save Yourself" by Stabbing Westward, Maxx flirts with the front-office secretary while collecting his USCW ID pass, physical and drug test, then says the fed puts "The Superstar" through too much to wrestle, that his first match, against Willy Vanilly, will not last four seconds, and that he finishes with the Double-X Plex (a slingshot backsuplex) and the Superstar Kick.
caption: A cocky newcomer who predicts his USCW debut against Willy Vanilly will last under four seconds, in May 1998.

tenures.source: /promotions/rspwf/archive/uscw-flash-central-5-5-98-pt-2-1998-05-06.html (USCW Flash Central of 5 May 1998, Part 2)

name: "The Machine" Ron Matthews
notes: Known from two segments of the USCW Flash Central, served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/uscw-flash-central-5-5-98-pt-2-1998-05-06.html (5 May 1998) and /promotions/rspwf/archive/uscw-flash-central-5-12-98-pt-2-1998-05-13.html (12 May 1998). Working out in his home gym with his ankles fastened to a wall, doing ab crunches, he accepts Scott Dakota's challenge to an I Quit match at USCW Weekend Edition, blames referees for both of his losses (one thought Viper was SWA, the other could not count) and says he has finished the Ironman Triathlon on a broken leg and never quit; in the later page Dakota says that he and Matthews both uttered "I Quit" at the same moment.
caption: A stubborn gym rat who took an I Quit match with Scott Dakota and, by Dakota's account, quit at the same instant, in May 1998.

tenures.source: /promotions/rspwf/archive/uscw-flash-central-5-5-98-pt-2-1998-05-06.html (USCW Flash Central of 5 May 1998, Part 2) and /promotions/rspwf/archive/uscw-flash-central-5-12-98-pt-2-1998-05-13.html (Flash Central of 12 May 1998, Part 2)
